sentences.label: Lowering the risk
sentences.text: These add up independently, and these lower the risk: through this sum alone, compared with no chest pain symptoms, typical angina takes a typical patient's predicted risk from about 32% to about 2%, non-anginal chest pain to about 7% and atypical angina to about 14%; being a woman lowers it to about 4% and fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL to about 20%; and a higher maximum heart rate lowers it steadily, from about 37% at 118 to about 28% at 175 beats per minute (chest pain type and maximum heart rate also act through the heart rate gate, below).

sentences.label: Raising the risk
sentences.text: Each extra vessel coloured by fluoroscopy adds about the same, from about 32% at 0 to about 96% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher; a flat rather than upsloping ST segment raises it to about 81%; and ST depression on exercise, cholesterol and resting blood pressure each raise it steadily, from about 25% at 0 mm to about 55% at 2.8 mm, from about 22% at 193 mg/dL to about 50% at 308 mg/dL, and from about 21% at 110 mm Hg to about 48% at 155 mm Hg.

Through this sum alone a reversible defect on the thallium scan raises it to about 57% (the thallium scan also acts through the heart rate gate, below); older age raises it steadily but only from about 31% at 42 to about 32% at 66 years; and the model ignores chest pain brought on by exercise.

sentences.label: Rare results
sentences.text: Some rarer results also count (the model has little data on this, n = 15 to 17): a downsloping ST segment raises the risk to about 54%, and through this sum alone a fixed defect on the thallium scan lowers it to about 12%.

This part reads chest pain type, maximum heart rate and the thallium scan, and acts on 104 of 242 training patients, 24 of whom had heart disease; for the typical patient it acts on, the predicted risk is about 5% without it and about 2% with it.

Across the whole model, non-anginal chest pain lowers the predicted risk, and even more so without a fixed defect on the thallium scan: from about 32% to about 3% then, against about 12% to about 2% with one (the model has little data on this, n = 15).

Across the whole model, a higher maximum heart rate lowers the risk, and even more so with non-anginal chest pain, where it falls steadily from about 7% at 118 to about 2% at 175 beats per minute, flattening out near the bottom because the predicted risk cannot go much lower; for other chest pain types it falls from about 37% to about 26%.

Through this part alone, for most patients a higher maximum heart rate does nothing until about 168 beats per minute, then lowers the risk steadily, but for patients with non-anginal chest pain it lowers it steadily all along: for a typical patient from about 32% at 118 to about 29% at 175 beats per minute (the model has little data on this, n = 14).

This part reads only the resting ECG: signs of left ventricular hypertrophy take a typical patient's predicted risk from about 32% to about 31%, and switching the part off changes any prediction by at most about half a percentage point.

parts.name: heart_disease_logit
parts.original_hypothesis: Root: heart-disease logit at output 0 (sigmoid). Essentially logistic regression: 16 direct edges (ca +1.78, cp:4 +0.87, sex:0 -0.77, slope:2 +0.63, oldpeak +0.56, chol +0.54, thal:7 +0.50, trestbps +0.49, slope:1 -0.47, cp:1 -0.37, sex:1 +0.34, thal:6 -0.30, cp:2 +0.26, fbs:1 -0.22, thalach -0.15, age +0.03) carry logit SD 3.66 and train AUC 0.9343 alone (L2 logistic regression on all 26 inputs: 0.9355). The two children are added to the logit: heart_rate_nonanginal_gate (x -0.519; +0.006 AUC, the only consequential nonlinearity) and restecg2_relay (x -0.021, negligible). Eight inputs are unconnected, zero effect: thal:3, thal:4, slope:3, exang:0, exang:1, restecg:0, restecg:1, fbs:0 (exercise angina is ignored). Evidence (train, n=242): composed closed form; sensitivity and mean |SHAP| both rank ca first (0.16), then cp:4, sex:0, slope:2; full-model train AUC 0.9403, accuracy 0.897.

parts.name: heart_rate_nonanginal_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: Protective heart-rate gate, gated by chest-pain type and thallium. 2942 = ReLU(0.968 cp:3 + 0.571) is a non-anginal-pain indicator (2.09 for the 70 cp:3 patients, 0 otherwise). 3842 = ReLU(1.021*ReLU(0.688 thalach - 0.374 thal:6 + 1.028*2942 - 0.347) - 0.295) is read out -0.519 into the logit. The gate opens once max heart rate passes a threshold set by the other two inputs: about -2.3 SD with non-anginal pain (open for 66 of 68), about +0.78 SD for other pain types without a fixed defect (38 of 159), and never with a fixed thallium defect (0 of 15). Once open, each SD of thalach lowers the logit by 0.36 more (total -0.52 vs -0.15 closed), and non-anginal pain lowers it by about 1.1. Evidence (train, n=242): closed form from get_formula; gate open for 104 patients (disease rate 23% vs 60% when closed); logit contribution SD 0.45; removing it drops train AUC 0.9403 -> 0.9344, a linear refit on cp:3, thalach, thal:6 recovers 0.9378 (R2 0.87), so most of its value is the gating rather than the linear trend. It is the model's only consequential nonlinearity.

parts.name: restecg2_relay
parts.original_hypothesis: restecg:2 relay: 3607 = ReLU(0.997 restecg:2 - 0.016) is 0.998 for the 119 patients with left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG and 0 for the other 123, i.e. exactly affine in the binary input on the data. Read out -0.021, it lowers the logit by 0.02 for LVH: negligible. Evidence (train, n=242): closed form; entry-exit correlation 1.0; logit SD 0.01; removing it changes train AUC 0.9403 -> 0.9401.

ann_28.text: This part acts on 104 of 242 training patients (43%).
For a typical patient it acts on, it slightly lowers the predicted risk of heart disease from about 5% without this part to about 2% with it (on the training data only).
In the training data, 24 of these 104 patients had heart disease.

The model gives a lower predicted risk of heart disease if the patient has non-anginal chest pain than if chest pain type is something other than non-anginal chest pain, and even more so if thallium stress test result is something other than a fixed defect on the thallium scan: for a typical patient, going from chest pain type other than non-anginal chest pain to non-anginal chest pain moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 32% to about 3% if thallium stress test result is something other than a fixed defect on the thallium scan, and from about 12% to about 2% if the thallium scan shows a fixed defect. The model has little data on this: only 15 training patients (a fixed defect on the thallium scan).

Other effects: non-anginal chest pain (rather than any other chest pain type) lowers it; maximum heart rate depending on thallium stress test result lowers it slowly at first, then faster for most patients, but for patients with non-anginal chest pain it moves steadily; maximum heart rate depending on chest pain type lowers it steadily (on the training data only). The model has little data on some of these: only 15 training patients (a fixed defect on the thallium scan).

Smaller effects, each changing the predicted value only slightly: a higher maximum heart rate lowers it with nothing until about 168 beats per minute, then steadily for most patients, but for patients with non-anginal chest pain it moves steadily; a fixed defect on the thallium scan (rather than any other thallium stress test result) raises it; maximum heart rate past about 168 beats per minute lowers it with nothing until about 168 beats per minute, then steadily (on the training data only). The model has little data on some of these: only 15 training patients (a fixed defect on the thallium scan) and 14 training patients (of them, patients already past their fold).

ann_29.text: Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a slightly lower predicted risk of heart disease if the resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy (about 31%) than if resting ECG is something other than signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG (about 32%) (on the training data only).
This part barely changes the model's predictions (by at most 0.5 percentage points).

ann_30.text: The model treats a higher number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same: for a typical patient, it goes from about 32% at 0 vessels to about 96% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher (on the training data only).

For a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise (about 81%) than if the ST segment slopes up at peak exercise (about 32%) (on the training data only).

The model treats a higher ST depression on exercise as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily: for a typical patient, it goes from about 25% at 0.0 mm to about 55% at 2.8 mm (on the training data only).

summary.text: The model treats a higher number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same: for a typical patient, it goes from about 32% at 0 vessels to about 96% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher (on the training data only).

For a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted risk of heart disease if the ST segment is flat at peak exercise (about 81%) than if the ST segment slopes up at peak exercise (about 32%) (on the training data only).

The model treats a higher ST depression on exercise as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily: for a typical patient, it goes from about 25% at 0.0 mm to about 55% at 2.8 mm (on the training data only).

For a typical patient, maximum heart rate going from 118 beats per minute to 175 beats per minute moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 7% to about 2% if the patient has non-anginal chest pain, and from about 37% to about 26% if chest pain type is something other than non-anginal chest pain (it moves steadily for patients with non-anginal chest pain).
